prompts.text: What's a piece of technology you used as a child that now feels almost prehistoric?
Tell me about the first device you saved up to buy for yourself.
I find a working cassette player at a jumble sale. Which old recording would you want to hear on it?
A box full of printed photographs or a folder of little videos you made years ago?
Old technology often had charming inconveniences that people forget when feeling nostalgic.
The sound of an old telephone ringing can bring back memories you didn't know you'd kept.
What's a gadget you miss even though your phone can probably do the same job?
We discover a retro gaming console with two controllers. What's the first game you'd want to try?
Writing a postcard and waiting for it to arrive or sending a photograph instantly with a short note?
Have you ever found an old digital message that made you laugh at how differently you used to write?
What makes a public place feel welcoming enough for you to stay longer than planned?
Tell me about a quiet library, park or courtyard that you once discovered by accident.
A public garden with winding paths or a small library with comfortable reading corners?
The best public spaces somehow make room for both people who want conversation and people who want silence.
We're exploring a new area and find a community noticeboard covered in unusual events. Which poster catches your eye?
Free spaces that encourage people to linger deserve as much appreciation as famous attractions.
Do you enjoy visiting a place just to experience its atmosphere without buying anything?
We come across a free outdoor exhibition nobody told us about. What would make you stop and look?
A shaded bench near a fountain or a little book exchange tucked into a neighbourhood street?
Describe a public space you've been to that made you feel unexpectedly at home.
Is there an interesting story behind your first name, a nickname or what your family calls you?
Nicknames are often tiny biographies, even when the original reason has been forgotten.
I learn that your childhood friends use a name I've never heard. Do I get to know the story behind it?
Being called a familiar childhood nickname or choosing a new one that fits who you are now?
Tell me about somebody whose name you remembered because of the way you met them.
People sometimes say a name differently depending on where they first heard it.
What's the most creative nickname somebody has given a friend of yours?
We're reading a map and find a street named after a person. What would you be curious to know about them?
A place named for its landscape or one named after an unusual local event?
Have you ever learned the meaning of a name and started hearing it differently?
What's a small thing you've repaired yourself that made you feel surprisingly accomplished?
Taking the time to fix a useful object can be more satisfying than replacing it.
A button comes off your shirt just before we head out. Who is more likely to know how to sew it back on?
Learning to repair a bicycle puncture or learning to mend a torn piece of clothing?
Tell me about a repair you attempted that went completely differently from the tutorial.
Every home has an object that still works only because someone knows its one peculiar trick.
Would you rather figure out a simple repair or ask someone who already knows how?
I offer to teach you how to tighten a loose chair leg, but my own screwdriver slips. Who takes over?
Restoring an old wooden table or bringing a neglected houseplant back to life?
What's a useful practical skill somebody taught you without ever calling it a lesson?
What's something you learned to do as an adult that made you wonder why you'd waited so long?
Tell me about a quiet personal milestone you didn't announce but felt proud of.
You finally complete a project you've been putting off. Would you celebrate or immediately start another one?
The feeling of finishing a long book or successfully making a complicated dish for the first time?
Not every achievement needs a photograph or a public announcement to feel important.
Sometimes the smallest sign that you've changed is how differently you handle an ordinary problem.
When you finish something difficult, do you like taking a moment to appreciate it?
I ask about something you recently accomplished and you brush it off as nothing. What's a fair follow-up question?
A little celebration with somebody who knows the backstory or a peaceful evening entirely to yourself?
What's a recent moment when you realised you'd become more patient with yourself?

productionNote: Fifty individually authored entries. Publisher quality screening required; human editorial review pending.
